# Notes for agents

- This repository runs Nintendo Switch games natively on Apple platforms: the game's own code runs, rewritten only where Apple's kernel requires it. Fifteen games are playable on the iPhone: Super Mario Bros. Wonder (update 1.2.1, profile `010015100B514000`), Fire Emblem Engage (update 2.0.0, `0100A6301214E000`), Metroid Dread (update 2.1.0, `010093801237C000`), 13 Sentinels: Aegis Rim (update 1.10, `01003FC01670C000`), Super Mario 3D World + Bowser's Fury (update 1.2.2, `010028600EBDA000`), The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild (update 1.9.0, SDK 20, `01007EF00011E000`), The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening (update 1.1.0, SDK 8, `01006BB00C6F0000`) Super Mario Odyssey (update 1.4.1, SDK 7, `0100000000010000`), Hades (update 1.0.38233, SDK 9, `0100535012974000`), Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity (update 1.3.0, SDK 9.6, `01002B00111A2000`), Fire Emblem: Three Houses (update 1.2.0, SDK 6.5, `010055D009F78000`), Super Mario Galaxy (update 1.3.1, SDK 18, `010099C022B96000`) The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom (update 1.4.3, SDK 20, `0100F2C0115B6000`) Monster Hunter Rise (update 16.0.2, SDK 11.4.3, `0100B04011742000`) and Ace Attorney Investigations Collection (update 1.0.0.2, SDK 17.5.3, `010005501E68C000`). Hades renders with Vulkan, which the host implements on Metal (`dm/gfx/vk/hle_vk.m`, profile key `graphics vulkan`). Age of Calamity is Koei Tecmo's KTGL engine: files in RDB archives, shaders as GLSLC outputs (`shader_split.py` `idrk_shaders`). Three Houses is KTGL too; 9 of its shaders exist only as compiles of the game's own GLSLC at run time, captured once on the Mac (profile key `shader_glslc_capture`). Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom run at 60 fps through a frame step the host decides in whole vsyncs (`patch_nso.py` `FRAME_STEP`, `nvn_fstep.h`, profile keys `fps_target` and `frame_step`); Tears of the Kingdom has a 5 GB guest layout. Monster Hunter Rise is Capcom's RE Engine: files in KPKA PAK archives (`shader_split.py` `kpka_jobs`, shaders in SDF files), the base game an XCI, its GPU heap a 64 GB sparse virtual pool (`hle_nvn.c` `vpool_*`, a 4 KB page table the replay reads textures through); it runs at 60 fps (30 on the Switch). Super Mario Galaxy is the Wii game on NERD's Hagi layer (PowerPC code recompiled into `main`), renders with Vulkan, and generates its shaders at run time, which the NSP script captures on the Mac (profile key `shader_vk_capture`); its pointer is the touch screen in handheld mode (profile key `op_mode`). Ace Attorney Investigations Collection is Unity 2022 IL2CPP: its shaders keep their parameters as blob entries of their own (`shader_split.py` `unity_code_blobs`), and its C# file API goes through the SDK's C library, whose path checks the host answers (`hle_fs.c` `IsPathMounted` and the length limits). [README.md](README.md) is the player-facing page (games, packing, playing); [docs/development.md](docs/development.md) has the internals, the script's options, building by hand, prewarm lists and per-game notes.
- Each game's constants and shader tables form a game profile in `dm/games/<id>/`, where `<id>` is the base game's title ID: `game.tsv` plus the tables and `dmsh_chain.h`. Mario's profile is `010015100B514000`. Tools pick the profile with `DM_GAME`; `make -C dm/host` and `build_ipa.sh` pick it with `GAME`. There is no default game: set it every time (the tools stop and list the profiles otherwise). Put per-game values in the profile, not in code ([dm/games/README.md](dm/games/README.md)).
- Per-build knowledge is keyed by the NSO build ID: rewriter cuts in `dm/tools/patch_nso.py`, the profile's `build` rows (the builds the NSP script accepts, and their display versions), and host behaviour that uses fixed module addresses checks `module_t.build_id` (from `fixups.tsv`; `dm_main_build()`, `DM_D2R_BUILD` for code inherited from D2R). When a new game build appears, carry addresses over with `dm/tools/nso_fnmap.py` and check them by disassembly; never let fixed addresses run on a build they were not found in.
- To analyse or port **another** Switch title, first run `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py` on its NSP folder. With no matching profile, it writes a survey to `<NSP folder>/<title ID>_survey/survey.md`, then a provisional profile guessed from the game files (`dm/games/profile_guess.py`; `<NSP folder>/<title ID>_build/profile/<title ID>/`, found by the tools through `DM_GAMES_DIR`), with a short heap check on the Mac when the game has virtual address memory, and a best-effort IPA that may not boot. Then follow [docs/agents](docs/agents/README.md) (extraction, binary survey, host bring-up failure catalogue, graphics specifics, debugging recipes) and add a profile.
- Scripts the user runs live in `scripts/` at the repository root (now `build_ipa_from_nsp.py`). Each one runs both in Spyder (F5, configured by the settings block at its top) and from a terminal (command-line options override those settings; non-zero exit on error). Tools that only agents or other scripts call stay under `dm/`.
- Game files, keys and anything extracted from them live in the game's NSP folder, never in this repository and never in the home folder (it is nearly full): the work folder `<NSP folder>/<id>-work` for extraction, runs and analysis, beside the NSP script's `<id>_build/`. Tool venvs and other large scratch data go on that drive too. Do not print key values.
- Language: everything is in English: `README.md`, docs, code comments, log messages, script output and other files. Red log lines (something unimplemented or wrong) start with `[RED] `. Text that must match a game's own Chinese data is written as escapes (`"\xE8\xB5\xB7"`), never as characters.
- After changing anything on the shader translation chain, run the chain procedure for each affected profile. The chain covers `dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_*`, `Program.cs`, the profile's `shader_map.tsv` / `shader_facts.tsv` / `shader_pairs.tsv`, and its `nvn_*` / `shader_*` keys. The procedure:
  1. Run `dmsh_chain.py --header`, which writes the profile's `dmsh_chain.h`.
  2. Rebuild the shaders (Mac and, with `IOSOUT`, iOS).
  3. Regenerate the profile's `c1_full.tsv`.
  4. Rebuild the host.

  The host only loads libraries of its own chain version. The translator is `dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_xlate_bin`, which matches `dmsh_chain.lock`; a fresh `dotnet publish` does not.
- iOS builds are unsigned IPAs that the user sideloads and tests; diagnostics come back as the app's `Documents/log.txt`. Do not sign or install builds on the user's devices.
- Commit only when asked, with `git -c user.name=seedds -c user.email=ext6@xcra.ai commit`.
